paper_metadata.title: Automated Construction and Growth of a Large Ontology
paper_metadata.venue: Doctoral thesis, Saarland University, Faculties of Natural Sciences and Technology
paper_metadata.abstract: This thesis presents an automated ontology-construction and growth architecture: YAGO as a high-coverage, high-accuracy core ontology; LEILA for extracting knowledge from natural-language text; and SOFIE for assessing plausibility and integrating extracted facts into YAGO, yielding an ever-growing, reconciled ontology.

problem_addressed: Automatically construct and continuously expand a domain-independent ontology containing individuals, a hierarchical class taxonomy, relations, and factual assertions, while minimizing human effort and maintaining high accuracy. The central Text-to-KG problem is turning Wikipedia and arbitrary natural-language/Web documents into canonical ontological facts that can be reconciled with an existing knowledge base.

methodology.description: Execution-order architecture: (1) construct YAGO from the September 2008 English Wikipedia XML dump and WordNet: parse Wikipedia pages; harvest infoboxes using a manually specified attribute-to-relation map with domain/range constraints; derive types and facts from category patterns; map category heads to WordNet synsets; resolve redirects, normalize values/names, deduplicate, and type-check candidates; export reified facts with witnesses. (2) LEILA preprocesses limited-scope text (encoding/format cleanup, sentence detection, date/number normalization, stemming), parses sentences with Link Grammar, optionally resolves third-person pronouns to the preceding sentence subject, induces positive and negative relation patterns from seed examples/counterexamples, generalizes them with adaptive kNN or SVM, and emits candidate binary relation pairs. (3) SOFIE adapts LEILA into a faster surface-pattern generator for arbitrary Web, Wikipedia, tables, categories, infoboxes, and note-like text; represents pattern occurrences and document-level word-in-context disambiguation priors as textual facts; creates hypotheses for entity senses, pattern-to-relation meanings, and canonical facts; grounds ontology/text rules; and selects a consistent, sparse set of true hypotheses through weighted MAX-SAT using FMS* plus dominating-unit-clause propagation. Accepted facts and optionally learned pattern meanings are added to YAGO for later runs.

ontology_or_schema_use.value: YAGO is both the target ontology and SOFIE's background knowledge. Its schema supplies classes, taxonomy, relation domains/ranges, functional-relation constraints, types, means links, and reified witness/provenance relations. Wikipedia infobox attributes and category regular expressions are manually mapped to defined YAGO relations; WordNet provides the upper taxonomy and synsets. SOFIE enforces schema constraints during inference, including domain/range checks and functionality, and supports RDFS-compatible export.

text_to_kg_stages: Text preprocessing: character and format cleanup, sentence detection, date/number normalization, stemming, tokenization
Entity and concept extraction: Wikipedia page titles, links, names, proper names, numbers, dates, and WordNet synsets
Entity typing: Wikipedia categories/infobox types plus WordNet hierarchy; domain/range and type-coherence checks
Coreference resolution: optional conservative third-person-pronoun replacement in LEILA
Entity resolution and linking: Wikipedia redirect resolution, canonical identifiers, WordNet linking, and SOFIE document-level word-sense disambiguation
Relation and triple extraction: infobox/category mappings, LEILA patterns, and SOFIE surface/sesquiary patterns
Ontology or schema discovery: category-to-WordNet class mapping and defined YAGO relation/schema construction
Graph construction: YAGO reification graph and canonical fact creation
Knowledge fusion and deduplication: reconciliation with YAGO, duplicate removal, precision preference, hypothesis integration
Graph validation and correction: reductive/inductive/type-coherence checks; SOFIE weighted logical constraints
Graph updating: accept SOFIE true hypotheses as new ontology members and reuse learned expresses facts in later runs

input_output.input_type: Semi-structured Wikipedia XML/HTML markup (infoboxes, category pages, redirects, links, article text), WordNet, limited-scope HTML/text corpora, and arbitrary unstructured Web HTML documents; SOFIE can also process tables, categories, and note-form text.
input_output.input_granularity: Wikipedia dump/article/page, infobox row and category string for YAGO; sentence and pair of words/mentions for LEILA; document-level word-in-context plus token windows (binary patterns default maximum length 6; sesquiary patterns default maximum length 3) for SOFIE.
input_output.output_representation: Canonical YAGO ontological facts/triples in a reification graph, including n-ary facts, relation domain/range-compatible entities or literals, estimated accuracy, and provenance/witness facts; exports include XML, relational database tuples FACTS(factId,arg1,relation,arg2,accuracy), and RDFS. LEILA alone outputs non-canonical word pairs; SOFIE outputs canonicalized, accepted ontological hypotheses/facts and optionally pattern-to-relation facts.

models_and_tools: YAGO extraction: XML-dump parser; manually designed attribute map (170 frequent infobox attributes) and category-map regular expressions; Wikipedia redirect resolution; WordNet synset linker; reductive, inductive, and type-coherence checking; RDFS-compatible reification.

LEILA: Link Grammar Parser; Unicode/HTML preprocessing tools; PlingStemmer; optional conservative anaphora resolution; link-grammar pattern features (bridge plus placeholder contexts); adaptive kNN and SVM classifiers implemented with SVMlight default parameters.

SOFIE: adapted surface-pattern and sesquiary-pattern LEILA; bag-of-words disambiguation prior over YAGO meanings; weighted MAX-SAT formulation; FMS/FMS* greedy solver with DUC propagation and on-demand clause generation; PostgreSQL for experiments.
datasets: YAGO construction sources: English Wikipedia XML dump from September 2008 (approximately 18 GB) and WordNet 3.0 noun synsets.

LEILA corpora: Wikicomposers (872 HTML documents); Wikigeography (313); Wikigeneral (78,141 random Wikipedia HTML documents); Googlecomposers (492 Web documents); Snowball headquarters subcorpus (150 text documents); Lonely Planet corpus used for comparison (1,880 files).

SOFIE semi-structured experiments: 100 random Wikipedia newspaper articles, seeded with 10 instances each for hasLanguage, ownedBy, and newspaperFoundedOnDate; 1,000 random Wikipedia articles of at least 10 kB for 14 frequent YAGO relations.
SOFIE Web experiments: 150 Snowball newspaper articles with 120 organizations; 3,440 non-Wikipedia HTML biographies retrieved for 400 randomly selected US senators (up to 10 biographies per senator).

metrics: Manual fact correctness/precision with Wilson confidence intervals for YAGO; 5,200 heuristic-derived facts assessed by 13 judges.
LEILA: precision, recall, F1; Ideal Metric for functional relations; Relaxed Ideal Metric for non-right-unique type relation; 95% confidence intervals.

SOFIE: manually constructed ground truth and standard precision/recall for controlled Wikipedia experiments; Ideal Metric precision/recall for headquarters extraction; manual precision-only assessment for large-scale Wikipedia and biography corpora; weighted MAX-SAT unsatisfied-clause counts/weight and approximation ratio for FMS* evaluation.
baselines: YAGO: informational comparisons to Espresso, LEILA, taxonomy induction, KnowItAll/KnowItNow, TextRunner, KYLIN, KOG, Ponzetto et al., and Alice; direct cross-system score comparisons are explicitly limited by task/source differences.
LEILA: TextToOnto, Text2Onto, Snowball, and the Cimiano–Völker context-vector (CV) system.
SOFIE: Snowball for the headquarters corpus; Johnson's weighted MAX-SAT algorithm, a simple greedy algorithm, and all-true/all-false assignments for MAX-SAT benchmarks.
evaluation.setting: YAGO precision was manually judged against the corresponding Wikipedia snippets, rather than an independent external ground truth. LEILA was evaluated on manually extracted ideal pairs from corpora and run on competitors' reported corpora/target relations to reduce tuning unfairness. SOFIE used YAGO background facts and rules with W=100 for inviolable clauses, w=1 for violable clauses, and ε=0.1 for Ockham's Razor; controlled experiments used manually compiled ground truth and seeded relation instances. Large-scale evaluations generally report precision only because complete ground truth was infeasible.

value: YAGO contains about 2 million entities and more than 19 million ontological facts; its manual evaluation reports 74 of 90 heuristics above 95% precision, including WordNetLinker at 95.11911% ± 4.564%, and the thesis characterizes overall accuracy as 95%.

LEILA on Wikicomposers type extraction achieved F1 45.03% (SVM) and 48.30% (kNN), versus Text2Onto 3.10% and TextToOnto 7.53%; on the Snowball headquarters corpus it achieved F1 63.81%/64.06% standard metric versus Snowball 31.72%. On the Lonely Planet CV comparison, LEILA F1 was 18.75%/19.26%, below CV-system 31.83%.
SOFIE on the 100-newspaper corpus using binary patterns reached precision/recall of 100%/97.75% for foundedOnDate, 96.55%/62.22% for hasLanguage, and 100%/85.96% for ownedBy.

SOFIE's random-1,000-Wikipedia-article evaluation produced 273 outputs, 238 correct, for 87.18% total precision. On 3,440 senator-biography HTML files it produced 744 outputs, 673 correct, for 90.45% total precision; diedIn was poor at 13.79% (4/29).

On the controlled Snowball headquarters corpus, SOFIE with the inverse functional relation attained 91.30% Ideal-Metric precision and 31.08% recall, versus Snowball's 56.69% precision and 30.89% recall in the reported comparison. FMS* left 241 violable clauses unsatisfied versus Johnson's 2,357 on the SOFIE biography setting, with no inviolable clauses unsatisfied for either.

value: Review-level inference: The architecture covers an unusually broad Text-to-KG chain—from semi-structured extraction and ontology construction through text extraction, canonicalization, logical validation, fusion, and updating—rather than stopping at non-canonical relation pairs.

Review-level inference: Defined relation schemas, domain/range/type/functionality constraints, canonical IDs, and provenance make extracted facts usable as a maintained knowledge graph and provide interpretable quality controls.

Review-level inference: The evidence supports high precision in several settings, especially curated/semi-structured data and canonical headquarters extraction, while evaluations also expose cases where recall or precision drops; this is more informative than a single aggregate score.

Review-level inference: SOFIE's unified hypotheses allow evidence from disambiguation, patterns, existing facts, and constraints to interact, enabling reconsideration rather than irrevocable isolated decisions.

value: Review-level inference: The approach depends on manually supplied schema mappings, category heuristics, seed facts/counterexamples, and axiomatic constraints; therefore portability and coverage are constrained by knowledge-engineering effort.

Review-level inference: Results are source- and relation-sensitive: LEILA degrades on heterogeneous Web corpora, and SOFIE's precision is weak for diedIn when patterns and constraints are insufficiently discriminative.

Review-level inference: The weighted MAX-SAT formulation is computationally nontrivial and uses an approximate solver; large-scale biography processing required 15 hours 50 minutes on the reported desktop hardware.
Review-level inference: YAGO source coverage is bounded by what can be extracted from Wikipedia infoboxes/categories, so high precision does not establish ontology completeness.

value: YAGO's extraction mechanisms are tailored to Wikipedia and WordNet; its content is limited to what could be extracted from Wikipedia infoboxes and categories.

LEILA extracts words rather than canonical entities, needs a disambiguation process to produce ontological facts, requires counterexamples for each target relation, and performs weakly on inhomogeneous random Internet text.

SOFIE's surface-pattern adaptation omits LEILA's deep linguistic analysis for throughput and non-sentential input; this harms difficult wording, pronoun/noun-phrase references, and relation connections across a document.

SOFIE does not resolve many references, has no quantifiers in its current MAX-SAT rule model, requires hand-provided axiomatic information, and can prematurely accept erroneous pattern meanings in batches before counterevidence arrives.

value: Author-stated: Discover relations automatically rather than requiring them by hand; acquire knowledge from new sources; develop new extraction models, reasoning mechanisms, and ways to combine existing knowledge.

Author-stated: For SOFIE, add richer textual facts (co-occurrence, document topic, style/language), source-specific information such as defining noun phrases, alternative pattern representations, and probabilistic, fuzzy-logic, or Markov-logic inference.

Author-stated: Improve unstructured-document recall using linguistic processing, anaphora and noun-phrase resolution; use document-topic/sesquiary strategies cautiously; exploit redundancy across documents; and add temporal reasoning.

Review-level inference: Future implementations could separate reliability calibration and relation-specific error analysis from global precision, because reported performance varies sharply by relation and corpus.

value: Author-stated: Automatically discovering relations and expanding beyond the initial knowledge sources remain open problems.

Author-stated: Canonical entity disambiguation and reference resolution in heterogeneous, arbitrary Web documents remain unresolved, particularly for ambiguous names, pronouns, family names, and descriptive noun phrases.

Author-stated: Selecting the correct relation for a pattern that can coincide with multiple relations remains unresolved; enforcing a single relation per pattern would fix some errors but wrongly prohibit valid type-dependent reuse.
Author-stated: Scalable, expressive reasoning with quantified/temporal constraints and incomplete/noisy ontology types remains unresolved.

Review-level inference: The paper's evaluations leave open how the architecture generalizes to modern domains, languages, extraction schemas, and independently verified ground truth, because all reported sources and methods are from the paper's 2009 setting.

code_and_data_availability: The thesis states that preprocessing tools were available as Java Tools at an MPII download URL and that YAGO conversion/loading software is provided; it also states an intention to make the YAGO, LEILA, and SOFIE code toolkit publicly available. The PDF does not provide a repository, license, persistent code archive, or reproducible release for the full experimental corpora.
